messages:
Priya Singh: Heads-up — FinLedger POC asking for a reserved-commit proposal. Requirements we got: sustained ~120 RPS text-gen, spikes up to ~600 RPS (5x) for short windows, ~3 AZs, encryption at rest + customer-managed KMS, 12-month reserved GPU ask. Need: recommended reserved GPU count, autoscale fallback plan, latency p95 target (they want <300ms p95 if possible), and a first-pass pricing sketch. Call with procurement Monday 10am PT.

Jamal Rivera: Quick Qs — what model(s) are they planning to run? avg/median token lengths? concurrency patterns (many short chats or fewer long ones)? do they require chat KV caching across requests?

Priya Singh: Customer said they want a 70B open model (LLM-70B family) quantized, median reply ~120 tokens, ~5% of requests are long (~1k tokens). Concurrency: most requests are single-turn web calls, not sustained multi-turn sessions. KV cache desired for chat continuity but not mandatory for first phase.

Marco Chen: Ballpark compute notes: 70B 4-bit quant on A100-style nodes => ~10-12 RPS per GPU for single-turn generation at median tokens if batching small. With KV cache and optimized kernels you might get to ~14 RPS under ideal batching. For sustained 120 RPS I'd recommend reserving 10 GPUs as baseline + 20% safety = 12 reserved GPUs. That covers steady load with target_util ~65-70%.

Marco Chen: For spikes (5x -> 600 RPS) we should use a mixture: prewarmed burst pool (on-demand reserved burst capacity) sized for ~50% spike, and autoscale into spot/ondemand for the rest with graceful degradation policy. We should avoid cold launches during short spikes.

Elena Ortiz: Proposed autoscale snippet (first draft):
```
policy: 
  target_util_pct: 65
  prewarm_pct: 30   # reserve 30% of baseline as prewarm pool
  burst_on_demand_pct: 25
  max_scale_factor: 6  # allow up to 6x capacity on bursts
  cooldown_sec: 60
```
This gives deterministic baseline + predictable prewarm cost, + on-demand for unpredictable tails.

Priya Singh: Pricing ask from buyer: what is monthly committed cost + marginal cost for burst usage? Need simple line items for procurement.

Marco Chen: Very rough numbers (ballpark) — use for procurement conversation only:
- Reserved GPU list price equivalent: $6,000 / GPU / month -> 12 GPUs = $72,000 / month committed.
- On-demand burst (short windows) effective cost ~ $9,000 / GPU / month equivalent (but billed by usage hours).
- Expected token volume (steady): 120 RPS * 120 tokens/request * 2,592,000 sec/month ~ 37.3B tokens/month.
- If we map that to unit economics, reserved capacity reduces per-token infra cost by ~30-40% vs pure on-demand. Exact per-token price we can give when legal signs pricing table.

Elena Ortiz: Runbook bullets to include in the doc:
- Prewarm schedule: 30% baseline across business hours, scale down off-hours.
- Canary rollout: 10% traffic to new model for 15 min, check latency & error rates.
- AZ failover: immediate routing to other AZs + instruct autoscale to spin replacement nodes, notify oncall.
- Fallback policy: degrade to smaller model or reduced max_tokens when p95 > 500ms.

Jamal Rivera: Two engineering asks before Monday: 1) confirm 12 GPU reserve meets their p95 at 120 RPS with 120 tokens median (can we run a microbenchmark on our staging config?), 2) a simple cost-vs-latency table for 8/10/12/16 GPUs so procurement can compare.

Marco Chen: I can run a quick perfbench on staging tomorrow — will post numbers. Also will produce the cost/latency table for the configs Jamal listed.

Tom (infra-bot): autoscale-policy draft "finledger-poc-v1" applied to staging (id: ap-7891).

Priya Singh: Thanks — action items: Marco to bench & produce table, Elena to draft runbook + pricing slide, Jamal to join procurement call for technical Qs. I'll book Monday 10am PT and share calendar invite + prod/infra slides.

Elena Ortiz: I put a stub deck in the deal folder: /deals/FinLedger/poc-capacity-sketch.pptx — please add numbers once Marco posts them.

Priya Singh: Perfect. @Marco Chen ping me when bench completes so I can attach numbers to the procurement email.
